title: Capacity signal HC phasing and price corridor schematic
content:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to tie explicit capacity signals to a phased hiring plan and a three-band pricing corridor. Goal is a small set of operational triggers (utilization, 95p latency, token surge) that map to concrete hiring or price moves so we can protect margin without over-committing headcount.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
We propose a staged headcount ramp across infra, serving-runtime, and SRE plus a lightweight sales support cushion. Hiring is gated by capacity signals. A three-band price corridor (base, defensive +15%, growth -10%) is simulated against three demand scenarios (steady, surge, structural growth) to show break-even deltas vs marginal GPU and FTE cost. Net: with the recommended gating rules, we can absorb ~2.2x short-term surge via burst reserve and temporary credits, and preserve margin in a sustained +40% demand scenario by selectively pausing non-critical hires and enacting a +10-15% price adjustment.

High-level assumptions (explicit):
- Base token unit cost to Redwood: $0.00008 per token served (compute+storage amortized).
- Average fully-burdened FTE (eng/infra/ops): $220k/year. Sales/CS FTE: $160k/year.
- One infra/platform hire increases sustained capacity handling by ~3.5% on our median request mix (assumption from infra bench).
- Burst reserve (prepaid GPU pool) can handle a 1.5x token surge for 6 weeks at effective marginal cost = 1.8x base token cost.
- Pricing elasticity: assumed take rate drop of 6% per 10% price increase in experiments (customer mix weighted).
- Planning horizon: next 8 quarters (Q1 2026 through Q4 2027).

Headcount phasing (staged hires with signal gates):
Inline table: Quarter | Role | Hires planned | Hiring gate signal
Q1 2026 | infra-engineer | 2 | sustained GPU util > 82% for 4 weeks OR 95p latency degradation > 10% vs baseline
Q2 2026 | serving-runtime | 3 | KV cache hit rate < 70% on cross-customer traffic + request tail latency rising
Q3 2026 | SRE | 1 | error budget burn rate > 1.2x for 2 consecutive sprints
Q3 2026 | sales-engineer | 2 | top-10 customer token commit conversion > 60% (onboarding pipeline)
Q4 2026 | infra-engineer | 1 | sustained demand growth >= 20% quarter-over-quarter
Q1 2027 | product-ops (part-time) | 0.5 FTE | feature rollout cadence needs support (qualitative veto)

Total incremental hires (year 1 ramp): infra 3, serving-runtime 3, SRE 1, sales 2, product-ops 0.5 -> blended run-rate delta ~ $1.4M annualized.

Simplified cost and throughput sensitivities (table):
Scenario | Demand delta | Burst used | Additional FTEs activated | Effective token cost | Revenue impact vs baseline
Steady | +0% | none | hires as planned (phased) | $0.00008 | +0%
Surge-short | +120% for 6 weeks | burst reserve 100% | hiring paused (use contractors) | $0.00014 | +30% revenue but margin compresses unless price corridor used
Sustained-growth | +40% qtr-over-qtr | partial burst then capacity hires | infra +2, serve +2 | $0.000095 | revenue +70%, margin improves if price raised by +10%

Break-even price calc (narrative):
- If sustained token volume increases 40% and we add 4 hires (avg cost $220k) plus amortized GPU increase, unit marginal cost rises ~18%. To keep current gross margin we need a price increase approximately equal to marginal cost delta (~+18%). Given elasticity assumptions, a +15% price yields ~9% take reduction but still preserves overall revenue growth and margin vs adding all hires immediately.

Price corridor design (three bands):
- Growth band (promotional): -10% price from baseline for selective segments to accelerate adoption. Use only when QoS headroom > 30% (utilization < 65%, cache hit >75%).
- Base band (status quo): no change to prices.
- Defensive band (conserve margin): +10–15% price across new enterprise contracts and renewal window when sustained baseline utilization > 80% or 95p latency slips and projected runway risk appears. Apply to new customers first and delayed renewals for existing customers.

Operational triggers and sequence (stepwise rules):
1) Monitoring signal: 7-day rolling median GPU utilization crosses 75% -> exercise autoscale/OOM tuning and enable priority queue for enterprise routes.
2) If 7-day rolling median crosses 82% AND 95p latency increases > 8% -> open hiring gate for infra/serving hires and spin up burst reserve.
3) If error budget burn >1.2x or incident count spikes -> pause non-critical hiring (sales/prod-ops) and fast-track SRE hire.
4) If sustained qtr-over-qtr demand growth > 25% projected -> trigger defensive band pricing review and conservative hiring plan (stagger hires 6–10 weeks).
5) If customer churn signal increases after price move -> revert individual customer prices and evaluate credits; only escalate to company-wide corridor after cohort analysis.

Micro-sim example (numbers):
Base monthly tokens: 1.2B tokens -> base compute cost $96k/mo (1.2B * $0.00008).
Sustained +40% -> 1.68B tokens -> base compute cost = $134.4k/mo.
Add 4 FTE annualized cost = $880k/year -> $73.3k/mo.
Total monthly cost rise = $111.7k -> per-token marginal rise = $111.7k / 1.68B ~= $0.000066 -> new per-token cost = $0.000146 (vs original $0.00008) -> +82% unit cost; this is a stress-case including conservative amortization.
Note: our more granular kernel/quantization recommendations reduce that gap by ~25% in model-heavy routes per Optimize team estimates.

Recommended immediate actions (next 4 weeks):
- Adopt gating rules in the Console as watch-only alerts (priority queue + hiring gates). Assign SRE/infra leads to threshold owners (Ben/Elena).
- Create a short-term contractor bench playbook: vetted infra contractors and pre-approved rates for 6–12 week surges.
- Draft customer communication templates for defensive band (scripts for renewals and enterprise sales).
- Run a refactor of per-route cost attribution to better measure kernel-level savings (link to cost-model PR in linked_artifacts).

Open questions / risks / notes: 
- Elasticity assumptions are noisy; cohort-level experiments recommended before broad price moves.
- Burst reserve economics depend on regional GPU availability; need infra to validate effective cost multiplier.
- Hiring lead times vary by role and geography; the gating rules must include minimum notice windows to hiring partners.
- Legal input required for price corridor language in enterprise contracts (preventing churn/legal pushback).

Versioning / next steps:
- This is a draft for finance+infra review. Incorporate infra capacity validation and sales feedback; update the micro-sim with live per-route telemetry by May sprint.

Appendix (compact tables for copy/paste):

Q2-2026,serving-runtime,3,cache_hit<70%,$660000

Q3-2026,sales-engineer,2,top10_conversion>$160k,$320000
Q4-2026,infra-engineer,1,demand>=20%,$220000

Sensitivity scenarios CSV:
Scenario,Demand_delta,Burst_multiplier,FTE_add,Effective_unit_cost,Revenue_impact
Steady,0%,1.0,as_planned,$0.00008,0%
Surge-short,120%,1.8,0 (contractors),$0.00014,+30%

End of sheet.
summary: Working budget/hc sensitivity tying monitoring signals to hiring gates and a three-band price corridor to protect margin under surge/sustained growth scenarios. Draft for finance+infra review.
